title: A Mixtape for the Prom
premise: Yara Kavanagh has spent four years perfecting invisibility at Bellhaven High, but when he finds coded instructions hidden in his late grandmother's recipe box, he learns she was part of a student group that exposed the school board's cover-up of a toxic mold scandal decades ago—and that the same corruption never stopped. Decoding her archive with the help of prom committee outsider Dev Okafor and his estranged cousin Priya, Yara discovers the board buried a new contamination report to protect funding for the stadium renovation. As the anonymous account he runs gets traced and his friends start paying for his curiosity, Yara must choose between safety and truth, broadcasting the evidence during the last football game's halftime show. The board falls, the school is closed for remediation, and Yara finally stops hiding—walking into spring with his name attached to everything he says.
about_author: Jude Galloway is a former high school debate coach who spent six years listening to teenagers explain exactly how adults fail them. They write from a small town where every school building has a wing nobody talks about.

chapters.title: Head Down, Grades Up
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. We meet him mid-routine: ace a chem test, eat lunch in the library stacks, post anonymously as @bellhavenleaks about a suspicious maintenance invoice. Establishes his rules of invisibility and the small thrill of the account. Emotional beat: controlled loneliness mistaken for peace.

chapters.title: The Recipe Box
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Clearing out grandma's kitchen after the funeral, he finds a recipe box where 'Cardamom Cake' decodes into coordinates and initials. The last card is addressed, impossibly, to whoever finds it: 'Finish it.' Emotional beat: grief cracking open into curiosity.

chapters.title: Locker Shut
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. He tests one decoded instruction—a locker number in the old gym—and finds a rusted tin with 1998 newspaper clippings about a mold outbreak the district called 'routine repairs.' First appearance of Dev, who catches him and assumes he's skipping class. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: The Committee Nobody Joins
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Dev, stuck running prom logistics alone after the popular kids bailed, ropes Yara in as his 'tech guy.' Their awkward alliance forms over spreadsheet drudgery while Yara hides the clippings in his backpack. Emotional beat: reluctant connection.

chapters.title: What Grandma Buried
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Researching at the county library, he learns grandma led a student group called the Ledger that forced a 1998 investigation—then went silent for twenty-five years. A librarian recognizes Yara's surname and goes pale. Emotional beat: awe and unease; his family history is bigger than him.

chapters.title: Priya
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Yara's estranged cousin, now student body treasurer, notices budget line items that don't add up—$400K routed to 'athletic facility remediation' that never happened. She confronts Yara, suspecting his account is behind an anonymous records request. Emotional beat: suspicion masking shared wounds from a family falling-out.

chapters.title: The Stadium Deal
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Prom planning collides with reality: the board votes to fast-track the stadium renovation before the last game, and Dev realizes the timeline exists to outrun something. He shows Yara the vendor contracts; Yara matches them to grandma's codes. Emotional beat: dread arriving on schedule.

chapters.title: Air Quality
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya pulls the facilities file and finds a 2023 air-quality report stamped 'resolved' with no follow-up testing—the same wing grandma's clippings describe. The three compare notes in Dev's car and realize the cover-up is generational. Emotional beat: the vertigo of a conspiracy becoming real.

chapters.title: Rules of Invisibility
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara wants to go slow; Dev wants to publish tonight. They fight, and Yara admits why he hides: in middle school, speaking up made him the target, not the problem. Dev challenges him: 'Your grandma wasn't invisible.' Emotional beat: the cost of silence named aloud.

chapters.title: The Trace
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The district hires a cybersecurity consultant after @bellhavenleaks posts the vendor names. Yara scrambles to scrub metadata and realizes the account's origin traces to the school network—to him. Emotional beat: paranoia closing in; invisibility failing by design.

chapters.title: Detention
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya is pulled into the principal's office over 'unauthorized access' to financial records—a warning shot aimed at her scholarship and college acceptance. She realizes they're hunting whoever is asking questions. Emotional beat: fear weaponized against the vulnerable.

chapters.title: The Ledger's Last Card
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Decoding the final recipe cards, Yara finds grandma's unfinished draft: proof the 1998 settlement included a binding remediation order that was quietly voided in 2019. The current contamination isn't negligence—it's a repeat offense. Emotional beat: inheritance transforming into obligation.

chapters.title: Homecoming Fallout
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. After Dev leaks one document early, his prom committee access is revoked and his mom's catering contract with the district is cancelled. Dev feels the first real price of involvement. Emotional beat: guilt and resolve tangled together.

chapters.title: What We Owe Each Other
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya, facing disciplinary hearing, nearly quits—but Yara offers to turn himself in to protect her. Instead she proposes they finish it together, properly: verify everything, then burn it all down at once. The trio formally becomes a team. Emotional beat: loyalty chosen over safety.

chapters.title: The Archive Room
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Following grandma's coordinates, they break into the sealed mezzanine above the auditorium and find the Ledger's old headquarters—decades of documents, including the original air tests and a list of board members who signed off across both eras. Two names appear on both lists. Emotional beat: standing inside history, holding its receipts.

chapters.title: Someone Is Watching
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. The consultant's investigation narrows; someone photographs the three leaving the auditorium wing. Dev receives an anonymous text offering him his mom's contract back if he walks away. Emotional beat: temptation delivered politely.

chapters.title: Fracture
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The group fractures over method: Yara wants the halftime broadcast, Dev wants legal channels, Priya fears any delay means the hearing buries her first. A bitter argument ends with Dev walking out with a copy of the archive. Emotional beat: trust stretched to tearing.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The superintendent summons Yara privately: full immunity for his friends, a recommendation letter, and the account deleted—in exchange for the archive. He mentions grandma by name, revealing the district has always known what the Ledger had. Emotional beat: the seduction of a clean exit.

chapters.title: Mixtape
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara declines, then builds the broadcast: a mixtape-style video splicing grandma's 1998 testimony, the voided order, the 2023 report, and the vendor payments, timed to the halftime show's audio system—which Dev, reinstated through a prom-committee loophole, still controls. Emotional beat: turning every skill of hiding into a weapon of exposure.

chapters.title: Last Game of the Season
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs interwoven. Halftime: the lights flicker, the jumbotron hijacks, and the mixtape plays to ten thousand stunned spectators as the consultant's men race the press box. Dev holds the door; Priya live-streams a backup feed; Yara stands visible on the field, name spoken aloud. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into triumph.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The state opens an investigation; the superintendent resigns; the hearing against Priya dissolves; the school closes two wings for remediation. Dev and Yara repair their friendship over leftover prom decorations, and the dance becomes a victory party nobody planned. Emotional beat: exhaustion, relief, tentative joy.

chapters.title: Signed, With My Name
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Epilogue in spring: Yara retires @bellhavenleaks with a final post signed 'Yara Kavanagh,' places the recipe box in the school's display case beside the Ledger's archive, and starts a new student watchdog group with Dev and Priya. Final image: a fresh index card in the box reading 'Rule one: be seen.' Emotional beat: belonging earned, memory honored.
